chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever dies on the road to Mecca, going or coming, is secure from the greatest panic on the Day of Resurrection.

key_terms.الْفَزَعِ الْأَكْبَرِ: The greatest panic (fear on the Day of Judgment)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for dying while traveling to Mecca for Hajj?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to emphasize the sanctity of the journey itself as an act of worship, not just the ritual performance. This assurance of safety from the 'greatest panic' (al-faz' al-akbar) during the resurrection highlights the divine mercy granted to pilgrims who die in transit, whether going to or returning from the House of God. It underscores the Shia view that intention and the state of being on the path to God confer spiritual protection even in death.
